handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, built, or decided in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

this_session.summary: Working session focused on fixing the highest-impact Stage 2 rule errors and Gemini extraction gaps identified in session 2026_6_10.1. All changes are in phase1/inference/m3_infer.py. No new scripts created. Also discussed LLM inference mechanics (prefill/decode, KV cache), ChatGPT critique of the extraction prompt, provenance-does-not-fix-hallucination, and whether single-pass vs multi-pass Gemini extraction is warranted — concluded: test first, restructure only if FH/MH counting is still dominant error after rule fixes.

changes_made.fix: Lot grading placeholder — flipped default from include-when-null to exclude-when-null
changes_made.before: lot_grading_in_scope=null → include LOT PREP EARTHWORK PLACEHOLDER scaled from analogs
changes_made.after: lot_grading_in_scope=null → omit from total, add Key Assumptions note with $X–$Y range for Brian to verify
changes_made.rationale: Placeholder fired on 7/7 jobs, was wrong every time. Null means the grading sheet wasn't present, not that lot grading is in scope. A range note is more honest than a wrong dollar amount.

changes_made.fix: Water main midpoint rule — trust plan read over formula average
changes_made.before: If plan coverage_pct and formula differ >20%, take midpoint and flag UNCERTAIN
changes_made.after: If coverage_pct not null, trust it as primary. Formula is sanity check only. If they differ >20%, use plan read and flag discrepancy.
changes_made.rationale: Plan read is a direct visual of actual pipe coverage. Formula is portfolio average. Midpoint was consistently pulling correct plan reads toward wrong formula values (Mountainside +28%, Painted Rock +54%).

changes_made.fix: Water main fallback formula — switched driver from road_LF to ROW_SF
changes_made.before: road_LF × 0.85 (hardcoded, references nonexistent item_scaling KP field)
changes_made.after: ROW_SF × qty_scale_correlations.correlations["8\" WATER MAIN PVC"].ROW_SF.median_ratio (read live from KP)
changes_made.rationale: ROW_SF is better predictor (r=0.992 vs road_LF r=0.934). Value now auto-updates as KP is rebuilt with new jobs.

changes_made.fix: Sewer main midpoint rule and fallback — same fixes as water main
changes_made.location: SYSTEM_PROMPT — Derivation Rule 4, SEWER MAIN LF section
changes_made.before: Midpoint when plan/formula differ >20%. Arc_loop override: road_LF × 0.80 hardcoded.
changes_made.after: Trust plan read when coverage_pct not null. Fallback: ROW_SF × KP median_ratio. Arc_loop gets 1.15× multiplier on fallback formula.
changes_made.rationale: Same root cause as water main. ROW_SF is best driver (r=0.944 vs road_LF r=0.687).

changes_made.fix: Sidewalk SF formula — replaced with sidewalk_sides field from Gemini
changes_made.before: road_LF × 5 × sides, defaulting to one side with no plan-derived input
changes_made.after: sidewalk_SF = road_LF × 5 (one_side) or road_LF × 10 (both_sides), driven by new sidewalk_sides field extracted from typical section. Null defaults to one side with Brian flag.
changes_made.rationale: Width (5 ft) and length (road_LF) are fixed. The only variable is which side(s), which is directly readable from the typical section cross-section. Mountainside was 4x over because the formula assumed both sides.

changes_made.before: Three triggers: (a) water main, (b) sewer main, (c) conduit in scope_notes
changes_made.after: Added trigger (d): estimate includes SINGLE DRYWELLS line item. Also fixed item_scaling reference → qty_scale_correlations.
changes_made.rationale: Lone Fir had $28K utility trenching in actual with no water/sewer scope — for drywell storm drain connections. Drywells always require trenched connections.

changes_made.fix: Stripping depth — read from plans instead of borrowing from analog
changes_made.location: SYSTEM_PROMPT — LS Item Inference, STRIP ROW + GEMINI_PROMPT_PDF + GEMINI_PROMPT_IMAGE
changes_made.before: stripping_depth_in always taken from analog's scale_metrics. Never extracted from new job's plans.
changes_made.after: New stripping_depth_in field in Gemini schema. Stage 2 uses plan-extracted value first, falls back to analog with flag.
changes_made.rationale: If analog was 6" and actual spec is 8", stripping CY was wrong by 33% on every job.

changes_made.fix: Image prompt — synced with PDF prompt
changes_made.before: Missing earthwork fields, road_LF_confidence, ROW_width_confidence, sidewalk_sides guidance
changes_made.after: Added earthwork_balance/import_export_CY/notes to schema, added road_LF_confidence and ROW_width_confidence, added sidewalk_sides bullet to extraction guidance.

this_session.knowledge_pack_finding: The system prompt was referencing item_scaling which does not exist in the KP. The actual scaling data lives under qty_scale_correlations.correlations. The best driver for both water main and sewer main is ROW_SF, not road_LF. This was already computed in the KP but not being used. All formula references now point to qty_scale_correlations and are read at inference time rather than hardcoded.

multi_pass_gemini_discussion.reasoning: Stage 2 rule errors account for 70-80% of dollar error. FH/MH visual counting errors (the main multi-pass motivation) are 20-30%. Running tests after today's fixes will show whether visual counting is still the dominant remaining failure mode.
multi_pass_gemini_discussion.proposed_architecture_if_needed: Two passes: (1) text/flags pass — current prompt for all non-visual fields; (2) utility-plan focused pass — targeted at utility plan page(s) at higher DPI for FH count, MH count, water/sewer coverage pct.
